questions.q: What is a force? Describe its effects and distinguish between contact and non-contact forces.
answer: A force is a push or a pull on an object, arising from an interaction between objects and measured in newtons.

answer.text: A force can set a stationary object in motion or stop a moving one, change the speed or direction of its motion, and change its shape.
These act only when objects touch. Muscular force is applied by our muscles, and friction is the force that opposes motion between surfaces in contact.
These act from a distance without touching. Magnetic force acts between magnets, electrostatic force between charged objects, and gravitational force is the pull of the Earth that makes things fall.

questions.q: What is pressure, and how do we experience atmospheric pressure?

answer.text: Pressure is the force acting on a unit area, found by dividing the force by the area on which it acts, and measured in pascals. For the same force, a smaller area gives greater pressure. This is why knives and nails are made sharp, while broad straps, a camel's wide feet and the foundations of buildings spread force over a large area to reduce pressure.

Liquids and gases exert pressure that increases with depth. The air around us has weight and exerts atmospheric pressure, which is very large. We do not feel crushed because the pressure inside our bodies balances it. Suction cups, drinking through a straw and the barometer all work because of atmospheric pressure.
